items.prompt: Türkçe ___ İzmir'e geldim. (I'm the one learning)
items.explanation: I came, and I'm the one learning. One person — just -mAk için.
I'm talking, you have to understand. Two people — -mA + the owner “you” (-n): anlaman için.

items.prompt: Çocukların ___ ışığı kapattım. (so the kids fall asleep)
items.explanation: The owner is the kids, third person: uyu + ma + sı. After a vowel, s steps in.

items.prompt: Geç ___ erken çıktım. (so as not to be late)
items.explanation: “So as not to” — negation -mA before -mAk: kal + ma + mak için. I'm the one who could be late — so no owner.

items.prompt: Daha iyi ___ örnek veriyorum. (so that you all understand)
items.say: Daha iyi anlamanız için örnek veriyorum.
items.explanation: I give the example, you all have to understand: anla + ma + nız için.

entries.text: Annemin dinlenmesi için yemeği ben yaptım.
Misafirlerin rahat etmesi için evi temizledik.

items.explanation: Look for the owner in the tail: -m, -n, -sı, -mız, -nız, -ları. Owner there — two people. No owner — the same person does it all.

exercises.instruction: Match the form and the translation

items.explanation: -mAk için — no owner. -mA + -m, -n, -sı — the owner is me, you, him. -mAmAk — “so as not to”.

exercises.instruction: Fill in the form, spot the mistake, build the sentence

items.translation: I drew you a map so you wouldn't get lost.
items.explanation: You're the one who shouldn't get lost: negation -mA + -mA + owner -n: kaybol + ma + ma + n.
I talk, you understand. You need an owner: (senin) anlaman için.

items.translation: I came so that you'd sew a shirt.
items.explanation: You sew, I came. Two people: dik + me + niz için.

items.text: Türkçe öğren___ için her gün dizi izliyorum.
items.translation: I watch TV shows every day to learn Turkish.
items.explanation: I watch and I learn — one person: öğrenmek için.

exercises.instruction: Tailor shop: for yourself or with a tag?
exercises.description: The student sees an English sentence and a verb stem. Step 1: “for yourself” (-mAk için) or “for someone else” (-mA + owner). Step 2 for “someone else”: pick the owner's tag. Right — the tag gets sewn on, wrong — the thread snaps and a “why” pops up. The logic is in index.html.

items.ru: I came to İzmir to learn Turkish.
items.explanation: Came and learning — that's me. One person: öğrenmek için.

items.ru: I talk slowly so that you understand.
items.explanation: I talk, you understand: anla + ma + n.

items.ru: I turned off the light so the kids would fall asleep.
items.explanation: The owner is the kids, third person: uyu + ma + sı.

items.ru: I wrote it down so I wouldn't forget.
items.explanation: I wrote it and I won't forget — me alone. No owner: unutmamak için.

items.ru: The teacher gives examples so that we understand.
items.explanation: The teacher gives, we understand: -mız.

items.ru: We're going to Çeşme to swim in the sea.
items.explanation: Going and swimming — us. Same people: girmek için.

items.ru: I stepped aside so you could take the photo.
items.explanation: I stepped aside, you take the photo: çek + me + niz.

items.ru: Mom gave me money so I could do the shopping.
items.explanation: Mom gave, I shop: yap + ma + m.

items.prompt: “So that you all get some rest” is…
items.explanation: You all rest — owner -niz: dinlen + me + niz için.

items.statement: “Bilet almak için gişeye gittim” — someone else buys the ticket.
items.explanation: There's no owner in the tail. The same person went and buys — me.

items.text: Herkesin duy___ için yüksek sesle konuştum.
items.translation: I spoke loudly so that everyone would hear.
items.explanation: herkesin — “everyone's”, third person: duy + ma + sı.
The negation sits inside: üşü + me + mek. No owner — same person.

items.prompt: Where does için just mean “for”, no goal?
items.explanation: senin için — “for you”, there's no action here. The other two have an action, so they have -mA or -mAk.
